newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to raise electricity rates in May - report.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to raise electricity rates in May - report.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has approved an average 30 percent electricity rate rise that will come into effect in May after being published in the official gazette, leading daily El Universal reported.

The cabinet "has agreed that the rises will come in increments and that the Electric Regulatory Commission (CREE) will meet next week to finally decide on the rates," Vice Planning Minister Armando Leon said, El Universal reported.
"The government won't decide on the final amount, the CREE will," Leon added in comments reported by the newspaper. Leon is to assume a new post on the Central Bank's executive board Friday.
El Universal said the rates would rise by an average of 25 percent in May, and then in 1.25 percent increments until the hike reached 30 percent in total.
Sources at the CREE could not confirm El Universal's report but said they had recommended to the government that some electrical utilities should receive higher rate hikes than others.
Stock market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas has long pressed for tariff increases, with market analysts expecting between a 15 and 20 percent rise for the company.
